instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines legislative 'actively advocate,' executive agency 'lobbying activity,' and retirement system 'lobbying activity' as contacts/direct communication to influence specified governmental decisions.

Each of the three lobbyist definitions ('legislative agent,' 'executive agency lobbyist,' and 'retirement system lobbyist') is defined as a 'person'/'individual' engaged to lobby, i.e., an individual actor rather than an entity registrant.
The definition of 'person' expressly includes state instrumentalities and political subdivisions such as counties, townships, municipal corporations, and school districts, i.e., public entities.
Lobbyist status turns on engagement 'as one of the person's main purposes' (and for executive/retirement, 'on a regular and substantial basis'), which is a materiality/substantiality threshold.
Executive agency lobbying is defined around influencing an 'executive agency decision' and direct communication with executive-agency officials within an 'executive agency' as defined in §121.60(F).

Executive agency 'expenditure' and 'financial transaction' definitions include 'a member of the staff' of covered officers, and 'staff' is defined to include executive agency officers/employees with policy/supervisory/funds authority.

The governor is explicitly included as a covered official in legislative lobbying definitions (e.g., veto/approval; expenditures; communications) and is an 'elected executive official' for executive-agency lobbying.
'Executive agency' is defined broadly to include 'any other state agency, department, board, or commission' controlled/directed by or subject to an elected executive official's authority.

Legislative lobbying is defined in relation to 'legislation' pending before the General Assembly/Controlling Board and 'actively advocate' is direct communication with members of the General Assembly or Controlling Board.
The legislative lobbying definitions include communications/expenditures involving 'any member of the staff' of covered public officers, and 'staff' is defined in §101.70(J).

The lobbyist definitions exclude certain elected officials (e.g., §101.70(F) excludes members of the General Assembly and statewide elected executives; §121.60(H) excludes elected/appointed government officers/employees acting fiduciary), so elected officials are not generally treated as lobbyists.

Public officers/employees are excluded from the executive agency and retirement system lobbyist definitions when acting in a fiduciary capacity, and §101.70(F) excludes various public officials, so public employees are not generally treated as lobbyists.
The statute includes specific public bodies within 'person' but does not define public entities by reference to a charter status or chartering test.
The statute's inclusion of public entities in 'person' does not rely on a government ownership/control threshold; it enumerates governmental units directly.
Nothing in the provided definitions bases public-entity status on how an entity is funded (taxes, appropriations, user fees); instead it lists governmental entities explicitly.
